items.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0
items.description: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0: voluntary guidance organised around four functions - Govern, Map, Measure and Manage - for embedding trustworthy AI in organisational risk processes

requirements.text: The organisation establishes and communicates its role, responsibilities and accountabilities for managing AI risk, and builds a culture for trustworthy AI including risk management strategy and inventory.
requirements.rationale: Accountability and culture are the foundation the other three functions depend on.

controls.description: Maintain an AI risk management policy naming accountable roles and a current inventory of AI systems.
Review AI accountability and risk appetite with leadership on a defined cadence.

requirements.text: The organisation contextualises its use of AI to understand the environment, needs and expectations of stakeholders, identifying and documenting risks associated with each AI system.
requirements.rationale: Risks cannot be measured or managed before the context they sit in is mapped.

controls.description: Document intended purpose, users and stakeholders for every AI system before deployment.

requirements.text: The organisation develops and implements quantitative and qualitative measures of AI system performance, including effectiveness, safety and reliability.
requirements.rationale: Measurement turns identified risk into evidence that can be acted on.

controls.description: Define and track measurable trustworthiness characteristics for each AI system, tested before and after deployment.

requirements.text: The organisation prioritises and implements risk responses, including treatment and mitigation, and monitors AI risks continuously across the system lifecycle.
requirements.rationale: Management closes the loop from identified and measured risk back into governance.

controls.description: Maintain a risk treatment register for AI systems with owners, due dates and continuous monitoring triggers.
Trigger reassessment when incidents, model changes or context changes alter the measured risk profile.
